code.originalText: Two-week review on the day of the cardiology consultation: the echocardiogram, stress test and calcium score, home blood pressure, a statin, and refereeing

text.paragraph: Two-week review on the day of the cardiology consultation. [S]

Mr. Leonard returns two weeks after intake and was seen this morning by Dr. Achebe-Lindqvist of cardiology, who did an echocardiogram, an exercise stress echocardiogram and a coronary calcium scan. The echocardiogram showed thickening of the heart muscle from high blood pressure with a normal pumping function, and the stress test showed no sign of narrowed arteries; his breathlessness at peak exercise came with a very high blood pressure rise. The calcium score was 186. He has taken losartan-hydrochlorothiazide each morning, and his home readings over the past week averaged 146/92 mmHg. He has refereed only short undercards, as advised, and has had no chest tightness on those nights. He is relieved that his license is not at risk and worried about the cost of another medicine. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1946-05-26; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Regular rhythm; sustained apex beat; fourth heart sound; no murmur at rest or with Valsalva; no edema

Breathlessness and tightness across the chest on exertion for about two months, late in long nights of refereeing in hot arenas, easing within a few minutes of rest; never at rest; no fainting, palpitations, orthopnea or ankle swelling; cause under evaluation with a cardiology consultation

S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to his documented work as a referee; superseded at the consultation when stress testing showed no ischemia and the symptom was attributed to hypertensive heart disease.

Stage 2 hypertension found at a yearly fitness examination for his referee's license (164/100 and 160/98 mmHg), with left ventricular hypertrophy by voltage on the ECG; untreated; home readings to follow
S — Synthetic diagnosis at intake; reclassified as hypertensive heart disease after the echocardiogram at the consultation.

Hypertensive heart disease without heart failure: concentric left ventricular hypertrophy (septum 13 mm, mass index 118 g/m2) with normal ejection fraction, grade 1 diastolic dysfunction, a mildly enlarged left atrium and an exaggerated blood pressure rise on exercise; no features of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
S — Synthetic diagnosis made at the cardiology consultation; not a claim about his real heart.

Coronary atherosclerosis found by coronary calcium scoring (Agatston score 186, about the 80th percentile for his age and sex), without angina and with no inducible ischemia on exercise stress echocardiography
S — Synthetic diagnosis made at the cardiology consultation; not a retrospective diagnosis of the cause of his death, which is disputed.
Hypercholesterolemia: LDL 160 mg/dL, HDL 44 mg/dL, lipoprotein(a) not raised; no diabetes

list.item:
Hypertensive heart disease (I11.9). Dr. Achebe-Lindqvist finds concentric left ventricular hypertrophy from hypertension, not hypertrophic cardiomyopathy or an athlete's heart, with normal systolic function and grade 1 diastolic dysfunction. The exertional breathlessness and chest tightness came from a steep rise in blood pressure on effort in a stiff, thickened ventricle, not from ischemia. Home blood pressure is still above target. [S]
Continue losartan 50 mg with hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg; send home readings weekly; dose review in five weeks.
Short undercards until home readings are below 140/90 mmHg, then full cards.
Water between bouts; stop and hand over a bout for chest discomfort, faintness or palpitations.
Hold the tablet on sick days and call.

Coronary atherosclerosis (calcium score 186) (I25.10). A calcium score of 186 puts him above the threshold where a statin is clearly indicated; LDL 160 mg/dL. Aspirin was discussed with him by the cardiologist and is not started while his blood pressure is uncontrolled. [S]
Atorvastatin 40 mg each evening from today; a generic at low cost.
Lipid panel at eight to twelve weeks.

Follow-up: Home readings weekly by phone. Seven-week review at the end of June with a basic metabolic panel; lipid panel at eight to twelve weeks. Next scheduled visit 1946-06-30: seven-week review: home blood pressure, the first weeks back at full cards, symptoms, and a dose increase. [S]
